subject: Biology
objectiveMappingPolicy: Official objectives are retained at topic level because the cited KIE syllabuses do not map each objective one-to-one to a numbered sub-topic.

source.authority: Kenya Institute of Education (KIE), Ministry of Education, Science and Technology
source.title: Secondary Education Syllabus Volume Two

objectives.label: a)
objectives.text: state briefly the general principles of classification of living organisms

objectives.label: b)
objectives.text: state general characteristics of each of the five kingdoms

objectives.label: c)
objectives.text: state the main characteristics of arthropoda, chordata and major divisions of plantae

objectives.label: d)
objectives.text: name classes of spermatophyta

objectives.label: e)
objectives.text: describe the main characteristics of classes of phyla arthropoda and chordata

objectives.label: f)
objectives.text: use observable external features to construct simple dichotomous keys of plants and animals

objectives.label: g)
objectives.text: use already constructed dichotomous keys to identify organisms.

subTopics.name: Main characterisitics of major divisions of plantae
Main Characteristics of the Phyla Arthropoda and Chordata (cover up to classes as shown)
Construction and use of simple dichotomous keys based on observable features of plants and animals

objectives.label: a)
objectives.text: define the terms ecology, habitat, biomass, ecosystem and carrying capacity

objectives.label: b)
objectives.text: identify the physical (abiotic) and biological (biotic) factors in a given ecosystem

objectives.label: c)
objectives.text: describe the inter-relationships of organisms in the ecosystem

objectives.label: d)
objectives.text: differentiate between saprophytism, parasitism and symbiosis

objectives.label: e)
objectives.text: explain the importance of fungi and bacteria as decomposers

objectives.label: f)
objectives.text: relate the mode of transmission to prevention/control of named parasites

objectives.label: g)
objectives.text: describe the adaptive characteristics of named parasites to hosts

objectives.label: h)
objectives.text: explain the importance of symbiotic bacteria in leguminous plants

objectives.label: i)
objectives.text: describe the nitrogen cycle88

objectives.label: j)
objectives.text: explain the flow of energy in the ecosystem

objectives.label: k)
objectives.text: identify and construct food chains and food webs, pyramid of numbers and pyramid of biomass

objectives.label: l)
objectives.text: explain the use of various methods of estimating population

objectives.label: m)
objectives.text: relate adaptations of plants to various habitats

objectives.label: n)
objectives.text: describe the effects of pollutants in air, water and soil on humans and other living organisms

objectives.label: o)
objectives.text: identify symptoms of different types of human diseases, methods of transmission and control.

subTopics.name: Energy flow in an ecosystem Food chains, food webs, decomposers, pyramid of numbers and pyramid of biomass
Adaptations of plants to various habitats
Effect of pollution on human beings and other organisms Causes, effects and control of pollutants in air, water and soil

objectives.label: a)
objectives.text: describe location and appearance of chromosomes and chromosome movement during mitosis and meiosis

objectives.label: b)
objectives.text: differentiate between mitosis and meiosis stating their significance in reproduction

objectives.label: c)
objectives.text: describe and state the importance of asexual reproduction, binary fission, spore formation and budding

objectives.label: d)
objectives.text: compare adaptations of wind and insect pollinated flowers

objectives.label: e)
objectives.text: describe the process of fertilization in flowering plants

objectives.label: f)
objectives.text: describe and explain how different fruits and seeds are formed and dispersed

objectives.label: g)
objectives.text: differentiate between internal and external fertilization as exhibited by amphibians and mammals (humans)

objectives.label: h)
objectives.text: relate structure of the human reproductive system to functions

objectives.label: i)
objectives.text: describe the role of hormones in human reproduction

objectives.label: j)
objectives.text: identify the symptoms and explain the method of transmission and prevention of sexually transmitted infections (S.T.Is)

objectives.label: k)
objectives.text: explain the advantages and disadvantages of sexual and a sexual reproduction.

subTopics.name: Chromosomes, mitosis and meiosis (mention gamete formation)
Advantages and disadvantages of asexual and sexual reproduction

objectives.label: a)
objectives.text: differentiate growth from development

objectives.label: b)
objectives.text: analyse experimental data on growth rates

objectives.label: c)
objectives.text: identify parts of a named seed and factors affecting viability and dormancy in seeds

objectives.label: d)
objectives.text: investigate conditions necessary for germination and distinguish the types of germination

objectives.label: e)
objectives.text: measure one aspect of growth in a given seedling

objectives.label: f)
objectives.text: determine the region of growth in seedlings

objectives.label: g)
objectives.text: explain apical dominance

objectives.label: h)
objectives.text: distinguish between complete and incomplete metamorphosis in insects

objectives.label: i)
objectives.text: explain the role of hormones in regulating growth and development.
